content_preview.title: AMD Ships FSR 4.1 Upscaling to Radeon RX 7000 GPUs Ahead of Schedule, Though Frame Generation Stays RDNA 4 Exclusive
content_preview.summary: AMD's Adrenalin 26.6.2 driver brings FSR 4.1 machine-learning upscaling to RDNA 3 Radeon RX 7000 cards using an INT8 model, but frame generation remains an RDNA 4 exclusive.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

AMD has extended its FSR 4.1 machine-learning upscaler to last-generation Radeon graphics cards. The company released its Adrenalin 26.6.2 driver on June 22, 2026, adding official FSR 4.1 support for Radeon RX 7000 series GPUs built on the RDNA 3 architecture, according to [TweakTown](https://www.tweaktown.com/news/112311/fsr-4-1-support-for-rx-7000-gpus-arrives-ahead-of-schedule-with-new-adrenalin-driver-update/index.html). AMD has now launched FSR Upscaling 4.1 for the older Radeo...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, tightly scoped News piece (415 words). Uses the Herald's Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure. Every factual sentence carries an inline attribution to one of the three cited outlets. Technical depth is appropriate and accurate.
editor_notes.source_verification: All three source snapshots read from disk and verified. source-0.html.gz (TweakTown, status 200): confirms Adrenalin 26.6.2 released ahead of schedule on Jun 22, 2026 with FSR 4.1 for RX 7000/RDNA 3; confirms the July deadline and 'at least eight days early'; confirms only upscaling was ported and frame generation remains an RDNA 4 exclusive; confirms 'same image quality as on RDNA 4 GPUs'; confirms RDNA 3.5 iGPU support 'in the future' and RX 6000/RDNA 2 support in 2027. source-1.html.gz (PCWorld, status 200): confirms FSR Upscaling 4.1 launched for RX 7000 (RDNA 3), originally planned for July, RDNA 2/early-2027 rollout, and RDNA 3 APU work. source-2.html.gz (Tom's Hardware, archive.org fallback, original 200): confirms the INT8-vs-FP8 statement verbatim ('FSR 4.1 for the RX 7000 series is based on INT8 code that differs from the FP8 instruction set that the RX 9000 series uses'), 'over 300 games', driver 26.6.2 on June 22 2026, and the enable path (toggle AMD FSR Upscaling in AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition / in-game settings). No misattribution found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific traces to a cited allowlisted source: driver version (26.6.2), release date (June 22, 2026), 'at least eight days early', INT8 vs FP8 model distinction, 'more than 300 games', RDNA 4-exclusive frame generation, and the RDNA 2/early-2027 and RDNA 3.5 iGPU roadmap. The article contains zero direct quotations, eliminating quote-fabrication risk. Confirmed the prior-review concern: non-allowlisted-only specifics that had been dropped (specific game titles such as the Doom/Assassin's Creed driver additions, the Jack Huynh quote, and APU model details like the RX 7800 XT) did NOT reappear in the body. The lone '9070' occurrence is the legitimate internal link to the existing prior article on the RX 9070 XT launch, which was verified to exist on disk.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. The Analysis section frames the software-vs-hardware feature-gap point without advocacy.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Herald article covers FSR 4.1 on RX 7000; grep of the articles collection returns none. Distinct from the March RX 9070 XT launch piece, which it appropriately cross-links as background.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: APPROVE. All three sources are on the allowlist and personally read from the committed snapshots; every claim, number, date, and technical specific is confirmed. No quotes to misattribute, no orphan URLs, and the previously dropped non-allowlisted specifics did not sneak back in. Ready for publication as-is.
